title: ON MY 52ND BIRTHDAY, I AM GIVING GOD THE ONLY GIFT I CAN NEVER TAKE BACK
paragraphs: ON MY 52ND BIRTHDAY, I AM GIVING GOD THE ONLY GIFT I CAN NEVER TAKE BACK
I am Brother John Asis. I am the Gospel Warrior. Today I am not celebrating how much life I have lived. I am standing before Jesus Christ and asking what I will do with whatever life I have left.
And strangely, the older I become, the less interested I am in pretending that birthdays belong only to us.
There may be food, laughter, photographs, messages, memories.
And I am grateful for all of them.
But somewhere beneath all of that celebration is a truth none of us can escape:
Another birthday means another year has been spent.
Another portion of this earthly life can never be recovered.
And today that truth is sitting heavily on my heart.
Because at 52, the question haunting me is no longer simply:
“Jesus... what will I do with the years I have left?”
I don't know how many there are.
Maybe that is why Scripture tells us to number our days—not because God wants us frightened of death, but because He wants us awake to life.
So today I don't want merely to receive birthday wishes.
I want to renew a covenant of surrender before God.
Not because God needs another dramatic promise from me.
Not because a promise earns His love.
Not because I can bargain with Him for another year.
But because His mercy deserves my response.
Paul wrote words that have become painfully beautiful to me:
“Παρακαλῶ οὖν ὑμᾶς... διὰ τῶν οἰκτιρμῶν τοῦ Θεοῦ...”
Parakalō oun hymas... dia tōn oiktirmōn tou Theou...
“I appeal to you... through the mercies of God...”
And then comes the language that changes everything:
That is what is on my heart today.
Lord, here is what remains of my life.
I have spent enough years learning that human plans can collapse.
Things you thought would last can disappear.
And eventually you begin to understand something you could not fully understand when you were younger:
Every day costs you one day.
And you never get it back.
So I don't want to spend the rest of mine merely building something people will remember about Brother John Asis.
I want whatever remains to point beyond Brother John Asis.
And I am the Gospel Warrior.
But please understand what I mean when I say that.
“Gospel Warrior” is not a claim that I am spiritually superior to anyone.
It is not an announcement that I possess every answer.
And I do not use this ministry to endorse one church, congregation, or denomination over another.
My focus is Jesus Christ, His Gospel, His Word, His teachings, and the call to follow Him faithfully.
The Gospel is not “come to Brother John.”
The Gospel is not “join my group.”
The Gospel is not “admire Gospel Warrior.”
The Gospel announces what God has done in Jesus Christ.
Grace is offered to people who could never purchase it.
And the same Jesus who forgives sinners also calls sinners to follow Him.
That distinction matters deeply to me.
but discipleship will eventually confront everything in us that wants to remain its own master.
“ἀπαρνησάσθω ἑαυτὸν... καὶ ἀράτω τὸν σταυρὸν αὐτοῦ καθ’ ἡμέραν...”
aparnēsasthō heauton... kai aratō ton stauron autou kath’ hēmeran...
Not once when the music made you emotional.
Not once when you walked to an altar.
Not once when you posted a Bible verse.
That is the Christianity I want to spend whatever years remain preaching.
Not Christianity as a social-media costume.
When you fall and must repent.
And when your eyes close here and open before eternity...
That is why my posts are often long.
Some people probably see them and think, “Brother John, this is Facebook, not a book.”
The internet has trained us to scroll quickly.
But some truths deserve more than seven seconds.
Some wounds cannot be addressed in three sentences.
Some questions have been tormenting people for twenty years.
Some believers are quietly starving while appearing perfectly fine online.
Somebody reading my posts may be sitting alone at 2:00 in the morning wondering whether God still wants them.
Somebody may have sinned again and be terrified to pray.
Somebody may be angry with God but afraid to admit it.
Somebody may have spent years inside churches while never truly understanding grace.
Somebody may be one paragraph away from realizing:
Jesus has not finished with me.
Because I would rather give someone enough context to understand than reduce sacred truth until it becomes another inspirational slogan.
Those who want something short can scroll.
There is no anger in that.
those who want to understand why they believe what they believe...
I want there to be something here for you.
And that is also why you may notice that the Gospel Warrior logos change.
There isn't one face of a Gospel Warrior.
The changing logos remind me that God works through unique human beings.
The Gospel does not erase your humanity and turn you into a religious photocopy of somebody else.
Maybe you have been looking at the words “Gospel Warrior” as though they describe somebody else.
Maybe you have thought a Gospel Warrior has to own a ministry.
Maybe your battlefield is your house.
Maybe it is raising your children to know Christ.
Maybe it is refusing corruption at work.
Maybe it is forgiving somebody who wounded you.
Maybe it is opening your Bible again after months of spiritual dryness.
Maybe it is telling your friend what Jesus did for you.
Maybe it is finally confessing the sin you have protected in darkness.
Maybe it is whispering through tears:
There are Gospel Warriors nobody on earth will ever make famous.
And perhaps that is exactly why the logo should never become the point.
At 52 years old, I have no desire to pretend I have arrived.
I still need the Holy Spirit to work in me.
And the older I become, the more dangerous I think it would be to forget that.
“Χριστῷ συνεσταύρωμαι... ζῇ δὲ ἐν ἐμοὶ Χριστός.”
Christō synestaurōmai... zē de en emoi Christos.
“I have been crucified with Christ... Christ lives in me.”
There is the great reversal of Christianity.
The Christian life is not ultimately about making Jesus a supporting character in the movie of my ambitions.
So on this birthday, I want to say something publicly so that someday, if I become tired, discouraged, wounded, misunderstood, or tempted to retreat into comfort, these words can confront me too.
If You give me twenty more years, they are Yours.
If You give me ten, they are Yours.
If You give me five, they are Yours.
If the road becomes difficult, keep me faithful.
If the ministry grows, keep me humble.
If the ministry remains small, keep me faithful.
If people praise me, remind me who deserves the glory.
If people criticize me, give me enough humility to examine whether they are right.
If I am wrong, correct me.
If I sin, bring me quickly to repentance.
If I become proud, break the pride before the pride destroys what You entrusted to me.
Never allow Gospel Warrior to become more important to me than the Gospel.
Never allow Brother John to become the center of something that belongs to Jesus.
And when my final day eventually comes...
let me have spent myself pointing people toward Christ.
And perhaps while reading this, something inside you has become uncomfortable.
Maybe because this isn't really only about my 52nd birthday anymore.
It is about your remaining days too.
You don't know their number either.
So let me ask you the question I have been asking myself:
If Jesus receives the rest of your life...
What person needs to hear about Christ?
What part of your life have you carefully marked:
Grace is not God pretending sin doesn't matter.
Grace is God meeting sinners who cannot rescue themselves.
The cross tells us simultaneously how serious sin is and how astonishing God's love is.
We were not redeemed because we cleaned ourselves up enough to deserve Jesus.
That is why our theme has become so precious to me:
Because Scripture is filled with people whose stories would make terrible religious résumés.
And then grace entered the story.
Christ transformed him into a servant of the Gospel.
The cross itself appeared to be the greatest scandal and defeat imaginable.
Death did not get the final sentence.
That is the Gospel Warrior message I want to keep proclaiming.
Your shame is not your savior.
But it does not possess greater authority than the blood of Jesus.
But they do not have to become your identity.
Your failures may explain chapters of your story.
They do not have to write the ending.
And if you have been hiding behind religious appearances, maybe today is your day to become honest.
Don't comment because an algorithm needs engagement.
Your honesty might become another believer's permission to stop pretending.
And if this article made you think of somebody...
“I read this and thought about you.”
A share can travel into a home I could never enter.
Onto a screen I could never reach.
Into the hands of someone I may never meet.
There may come a night when you need these words more than you need them today.
Invite the person who walked away from church.
Invite the lukewarm Christian who knows something is missing.
Even invite the unbelieving friend who is willing to listen.
Then let us keep bringing all of it beneath the authority of Scripture and to the feet of Jesus.
And for those who want to help Gospel Warrior continue doing this work, I want to make the invitation clearly without confusing support for this ministry with the Gospel itself.
You do not buy salvation by supporting Gospel Warrior.
You do not prove that you love God by giving money to me.
Salvation is God's gift in Christ.
But believers can freely choose to support Gospel work because they want biblical teaching and discipleship resources to continue reaching people.
But I want the deepest reason to remain deeper than merchandise.
And then don't merely support financially.
Test what I teach against God's Word.
Correct me if I depart from Scripture.
Point people beyond Gospel Warrior toward Jesus Christ.
Because not everybody can afford a shelf full of Christian books.
Not everybody lives near a Christian bookstore.
Not everybody has access to a theological library.
But if someone has a phone and a hunger to know Christ more deeply, I want Gospel Warrior to keep placing resources within reach.
That is part of what your support helps sustain.
And today, on my 52nd birthday, that matters more to me than receiving something for myself.
I would rather see another person open Scripture.
I would rather see a marriage turn toward Christ.
I would rather see a wandering believer come home.
I would rather see someone finally understand grace.
I would rather see somebody repent.
I would rather see one exhausted Christian whisper, “Jesus, I'm coming back.”
Because eventually there will be a birthday I will not celebrate on this earth.
There will be a final post.
A final prayer spoken with these lungs.
A final time I type the words “Gospel Warrior.”
And somebody else will have to carry the Gospel into the next room...
Maybe that somebody is reading this right now.
Maybe the reason this became such a long birthday article is because somewhere inside these words, God is reminding you that Christianity was never intended to be spectator religion.
You were called to follow Christ.
To become less impressed with yourself and increasingly overwhelmed by Jesus.
So don't make my 52nd birthday about me.
Turn it into a question about your own surrender.
What are you doing with the life God has allowed you to live?
You cannot return yesterday to God.
The person carrying memories nobody else knows.
The person who needs mercy again.
And the astonishing message of Christianity is not that Jesus waits until people become impressive enough to approach Him.
The Gospel says that Christ came for sinners.
And because the tomb is empty, surrender is not surrender to a dead teacher.
Not to make people disciples of Brother John Asis.
Not to spend the rest of my days asking:
“What can God do for my plans?”
“Lord, what do You want to do with whatever remains of me?”
Then live like you meant it.
do not leave without hearing the message that matters infinitely more:
And when your past whispers that your story is already ruined, look toward the cross.
When shame tells you there is no road home, remember the empty tomb.
When failure tries to write your final sentence, remember who holds the pen.
Because your darkest chapter may be real...
but scars become testimony when the wounded hands of Jesus are holding the pen.
